reading.body:
Tesla produces Tesla Optimus, a humanoid robot for factory automation where physical interaction with workers creates safety and liability considerations that differ from purely digital AI systems.

The emergence of physical robots in manufacturing represents a shift in where AI capabilities manifest. Optimus operates in the constraint space that matters most for AI scaling: the physical world of factories, where errors have immediate material consequences. This pushes the problem beyond compute allocation into questions of mechanical reliability, safety certification, and real-time decision-making under conditions that cannot be paused or rolled back.

For infrastructure planning, physical AI systems create different demands than data center workloads. A factory robot needs power at the point of use, not just at a data center. It requires physical space, integration with existing production lines, and ongoing maintenance. The grid impact differs from training clusters, but so does the question of whether compute itself is the constraint or whether physical embodiment, mechanical systems, and safety certification become the actual bottlenecks to deployment.

This data covers a product category and use case. It does not cover Tesla's broader AI work, energy infrastructure, or whether Optimus robots are currently deployed at scale or remain in development. It does not quantify compute requirements, power draw, or production volume.
